original_test_intent: Verify that the front-I/O-board USB-C receptacle is wired to the intended CPU USB controller/root port and can enumerate an approved known-good device at the required USB mode/speed without reset, overcurrent, orientation or signal-path faults.
original_method: Map the CPU USB controller/root port through board headers/cable and front-I/O-board connector to the exact USB-C receptacle; define Type-C role/orientation and any mux/retimer/power-delivery involvement; record baseline port state and errors; have an operator inspect/photograph the path and attach an approved fixture in each required orientation; capture complete topology/descriptors, negotiated speed/power and kernel events; optionally perform a bounded read-only fixture query; safely remove the fixture and preserve overcurrent/reset evidence without generic hub substitution or automatic reconnect/reset.
manual_activity: An operator identifies the exact front-I/O USB-C receptacle, inspects/photographs its internal cable and connector, and inserts/removes the approved known-good fixture in each engineer-required orientation.
required_inputs: CPU USB controller/root-port to board header/cable/front-I/O-board/USB-C receptacle map
USB-C data/power role, orientation coverage, mux/retimer/PD-controller path and expected mode/speed
Known-good fixture VID:PID/product/serial/class and any bounded functional read criterion
Safe insertion/removal procedure, overcurrent/reset limits, aborts and recovery
safety_requirements: Use only the approved fixture and port; confirm Type-C roles and voltage/current expectations before insertion
Do not infer an empty receptacle is detected; bind the fixture's stable identity to the exact CPU root-port path
Do not use unknown storage or network devices, write fixture media, force alternate modes, reset/rebind controllers or clear logs
Monitor overcurrent, repeated connect/disconnect, PD negotiation, speed downgrade and host stability
Stop and remove the fixture through the approved procedure on heat, overcurrent, reset storm, wrong route or instability; no automatic retry
agent_execution_scope: Validate CPU/front-I/O topology, Type-C role/orientation requirements, fixture identity and safe method
After operator insertion, collect complete topology/descriptors, speed/power and kernel/USB error evidence for the exact root-port chain
Compare required orientations and negotiated mode; perform only an approved non-destructive fixture query if specified
Do not substitute a BMC/HPM hub, select an unknown device, write fixture data, manipulate PD/controller state or issue the DUT verdict
engineer_actions: Approve CPU root-port/header/cable/front-I/O USB-C mapping and Type-C/PD/mux/retimer behavior
Approve known-good fixture, required orientations, mode/speed/power and error/overcurrent acceptance
Review physical and port-bound enumeration/function evidence and decide PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED

review_improvement: Corrects the reference's unrelated BMC/hub scope and turns vague port detection into a root-path-, orientation- and fixture-bound USB-C function test with overcurrent protection.
independent_technical_reasoning: A USB receptacle is passive and cannot itself appear in `lsusb`; detection requires a known device. The source also specifically names USB-C, where cable orientation, data-role negotiation and mux/retimer paths can fail independently. Therefore the case needs an identified fixture and exact CPU root-port mapping, ideally tested in required orientations at the specified speed. This is not a generic hub inventory check, and physical insertion means operator confirmation remains necessary.
